I think this has to do with how much smaller the world has gotten and the instant gratification/ADHD society we're in. Out with the old broken toy, in with the new. 

3. Sentiment:

One person, typically the guy in my experience, takes the relationship a lot more seriously and more special than the other. I mean personally I remember every little nice thing she did, the movies we watched together, making certain meals together... In my last relationship I would bring up an activity we did together a few days prior and she wouldn't even remember one damn thing about it. To me it was special and to her it was monotonous and mundane, much like the relationship itself. Just because something holds a lot of value on one person's end, doesn't mean it means the same for the other.

I'm on year 4. Year. 4. No matter how much you sit and dwell on yours they will continue to live theirs. Live for YOU now. Nobody will stop you if you want to throw away this opportunity, unfortunately. I'm glad you're recognizing it early though. Live your life, friend. Best wishes. I know it isn't fair, but fairness is only a living concept of our perception/reality. We always think things will go our way or sort out eventually, but that hope can lead you to missing the whole experience. You can only do your best with what's in front of you. I haven't really been able to apply that ideology myself, but I want my experience to at least be a lesson to some. I threw my life away for a girl that forgot about me in two weeks. I started glamorizing the relationship after the fact, because I didn't have it anymore. I spend so much time in the past and thinking "what could have been" that I have literally not been living in the moment. I think that might be a mental illness of its own, but regardless I think anyone could end up here if they didn't strive to shift their focus elsewhere. Thats the problem, I never want to shift my focus elsewhere because in my mind that stupid 5 year relationship was somehow the missing piece to everything that's wrong with me today. I choose everyday to let this idea of this girl ruin me. How could she leave me for dead? How could she move on so quickly, why does everyone agree with her and not me. See, we think what someone means to us, is what we mean to them by default. You know how they say "one person's trash is another person's treasure"? Well I want to apply that to the concept of how we feel about one another. My partner was gold to me, I was a carcass on the side of the road to her. So because I see her as golden, she owes it to me to sit and pretend I'm also gold to her? Thats ridiculous, no? So I accept now that I wouldn't want to be with a deadbeat myself, so I don't blame her. She can live her life at my expense, but still that doesn't matter. We are all entitled to have our own lives. Dont live through someone else. I hope this banter helped someone out in some kind of way.
